newsitem.title: USA: Boston Stock Exchange to relocate within city.
newsitem.headline: Boston Stock Exchange to relocate within city.

text.p: The Boston Stock Exchange said Tuesday it will relocate to another location in the city and expand its trading floor and the number of trading posts.

"For more than a decade, we have been one of the fastest growing securities exchanges in the country and this move will put in place the advanced technology and communications platform we will need for our next stage of growth," BSE Chairman William Morton said in a release.

The stock exchange will move from its headquarters at One Boston Place, where it has a 5,300 square foot trading floor, to 100 Franklin Street and to a 9,300 square foot floor. The number of trading posts at the new site where traders can input trades into workstations will be expanded to 142 from 92 posts currently.
In addition, a vistors gallery which will offer the public views of the expanded trading floor, and educational exhibits about the history of the BSE will be provided.
The move is expected to be completed by late 1998 or early 1999, said BSE spokeswoman Nicole Kalicki.
Founded in 1834, the BSE is one of the smaller of the seven stock exchanges in the country, with an average of about 12,700 trades totalling about 7.2 million shares daily.
